Every monitoring dashboard needs to break dates into parts: **year**, **month**, **month name** and, for
deforestation, the **PRODES year**, which runs from **August 1 to July 31**. "PRODES 2025" starts in
August 2024.

In the old scripts, each part was a function with an `UpdateCursor`, repeated across several files.
Here each one becomes **a single line** in each program.

![The PRODES year starts in August: August is month 1 and July is month 12.](../imagens/artigos/calendario_prodes.png){fig-alt="Two month rulers. On top, the calendar year from January to December. Below, the PRODES year 2025, from August 2024 (month 1) to July 2025 (month 12), with arrows linking the corresponding months."}

## The rules

The field names are in Portuguese, as in the dashboards: `ano` = year, `mes` = month,
`mes_nome` = month name, `ano_prodes` = PRODES year, `mes_prodes` = PRODES month.

| Field | Rule | 2025-03-15 | 2025-09-20 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ano` | year of the date | 2025 | 2025 |
| `mes` | month of the date | 3 | 9 |
| `mes_nome` | month name, from a fixed list | March | September |
| `ano_prodes` | year + 1 if the month is August or later | 2025 | **2026** |
| `mes_prodes` | August = 1 … July = 12, or `(mes + 4) % 12 + 1` | 8 | 2 |

`%` is the **remainder of the division**: `(9 + 4) % 12 + 1` = `13 % 12 + 1` = `1 + 1` = 2.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Month name from the computer's language
The old script used `strftime("%B")`, which returns the month name **in the system language**: "março"
on a computer in Portuguese, "March" on a server in English. In a dashboard, that mixes languages. Use a
**fixed list** of names, as in the code below.
:::

## The code

The examples use the `deter` layer (field `view_date`) of the articles' GeoPackage
([how to download](about.qmd#data)).

::: {.panel-tabset group="programa"}

## ArcGIS Pro

```python
import arcpy

fc = r"C:\dados\resultados.gdb\deter"
arcpy.management.CopyFeatures(r"C:\dados\artigos.gpkg\main.deter", fc)

meses = ("['January','February','March','April','May','June','July',"
         "'August','September','October','November','December']")

arcpy.management.CalculateFields(fc, "PYTHON3", [
    ["ano",        "!view_date!.year"],
    ["mes",        "!view_date!.month"],
    ["mes_nome",   f"{meses}[!view_date!.month - 1]"],
    ["ano_prodes", "!view_date!.year + (1 if !view_date!.month >= 8 else 0)"],
    ["mes_prodes", "(!view_date!.month + 4) % 12 + 1"],
])
```

`CalculateFields` (plural) computes several fields at once and creates the ones that do not exist. In
ArcMap, use one `CalculateField_management` per field, with `"PYTHON_9.3"`.

## QGIS

In the **Field Calculator**, create each field with the expression:

| Field | Type | Expression |
|---|---|---|
| `ano` | integer | `year("view_date")` |
| `mes` | integer | `month("view_date")` |
| `mes_nome` | text | `array_get(array('January','February','March','April','May','June','July','August','September','October','November','December'), month("view_date") - 1)` |
| `ano_prodes` | integer | `year("view_date") + if(month("view_date") >= 8, 1, 0)` |
| `mes_prodes` | integer | `(month("view_date") + 4) % 12 + 1` |

In the Python console, the same five fields in sequence:

```python
import processing
G = "C:/dados/artigos.gpkg"

campos = [
    ("ano", 1, 'year("view_date")'),
    ("mes", 1, 'month("view_date")'),
    ("mes_nome", 2, "array_get(array('January','February','March','April','May','June',"
                    "'July','August','September','October','November','December'), "
                    'month("view_date") - 1)'),
    ("ano_prodes", 1, 'year("view_date") + if(month("view_date") >= 8, 1, 0)'),
    ("mes_prodes", 1, '(month("view_date") + 4) % 12 + 1'),
]
camada = f"{G}|layername=deter"
for nome, tipo, formula in campos:          # type: 1 = integer, 2 = text
    camada = processing.run("native:fieldcalculator", {
        "INPUT": camada, "FIELD_NAME": nome, "FIELD_TYPE": tipo, "FIELD_LENGTH": 12,
        "FORMULA": formula, "OUTPUT": "memory:"})["OUTPUT"]

resumo = processing.run("qgis:statisticsbycategories", {
    "INPUT": camada, "CATEGORIES_FIELD_NAME": ["ano_prodes"], "OUTPUT": "memory:"})["OUTPUT"]
for f in resumo.getFeatures():
    print(f["ano_prodes"], f["count"])
```

## PostGIS

```sql
SELECT view_date,
       extract(year FROM view_date)::int                                   AS ano,
       extract(month FROM view_date)::int                                  AS mes,
       (ARRAY['January','February','March','April','May','June','July',
              'August','September','October','November','December'])
           [extract(month FROM view_date)::int]                            AS mes_nome,
       extract(year FROM view_date + interval '5 months')::int             AS ano_prodes,
       (extract(month FROM view_date)::int + 4) % 12 + 1                   AS mes_prodes
FROM artigos.deter
LIMIT 5;

-- Check: alerts by PRODES year
SELECT extract(year FROM view_date + interval '5 months')::int AS ano_prodes, count(*)
FROM artigos.deter
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
```

The `+ interval '5 months'` trick: adding 5 months to any date from August to December pushes it into
the next year, while dates from January to July stay in the same year. That is exactly the PRODES year
rule.

## Python

```python
import geopandas as gpd

deter = gpd.read_file("dados/artigos.gpkg", layer="deter")
data = deter["view_date"].astype("datetime64[ns]")

MESES = ["January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July",
         "August", "September", "October", "November", "December"]

deter["ano"] = data.dt.year
deter["mes"] = data.dt.month
deter["mes_nome"] = deter["mes"].map(lambda m: MESES[m - 1])
deter["ano_prodes"] = deter["ano"] + (deter["mes"] >= 8).astype(int)
deter["mes_prodes"] = (deter["mes"] + 4) % 12 + 1

print(deter[["view_date", "ano", "mes", "mes_nome", "ano_prodes", "mes_prodes"]].head())
print(deter.groupby("ano_prodes").size())
```

## Power BI

In **Power Query** (Home → Transform data), use **Add Column → Custom Column**:

```
// ano_prodes
Date.Year([view_date]) + (if Date.Month([view_date]) >= 8 then 1 else 0)

// mes_prodes
Number.Mod(Date.Month([view_date]) + 4, 12) + 1

// mes_nome (fixed list, independent of the language)
{"January","February","March","April","May","June","July",
 "August","September","October","November","December"}{Date.Month([view_date]) - 1}
```

Or in **DAX**, as a calculated column of the calendar table:

```
PRODES year = YEAR ( dim_calendario[data] ) + IF ( MONTH ( dim_calendario[data] ) >= 8, 1, 0 )
PRODES month = MOD ( MONTH ( dim_calendario[data] ) + 4, 12 ) + 1
```

To sort months in PRODES-year order in charts, select the `mes_nome` column and use
**Sort by column → mes_prodes**.

:::

## Checking the result

The QGIS, PostGIS and Python versions gave the same count of alerts by PRODES year:

| PRODES year | Period | DETER alerts in the study area |
|---|---|---:|
| 2024 | Jan to Jul 2024 (the download starts in 2024) | 639 |
| 2025 | Aug 2024 to Jul 2025 | 5,787 |
| 2026 | Aug 2025 to Jul 2026 | 595 |
| 2027 | Aug to Oct 2026 (ongoing) | 802 |

: DETER alerts by PRODES year, all classes. {.striped}

The 2025 peak is **5,127 burn scars** from the 2024 drought. Separating by class, clear-cut deforestation
alerts (`DESMATAMENTO_CR`) numbered 431 in 2025 and 300 in 2026. That is why dashboards almost always
separate **deforestation** from **fire**.

## First and last day of the period

Two other common questions: "what are the first and last alerts in the layer?" (for the report title)
and "what is the last day of the month?" (to know whether the month is closed).

| | First and last date | Last day of the month |
|---|---|---|
| ArcGIS Pro | `min()`/`max()` over `arcpy.da.SearchCursor(fc, ["view_date"])` | `calendar.monthrange(year, month)[1]` |
| QGIS | `minimum("view_date")`, `maximum("view_date")` | `make_date(year(d), month(d), 1) + '1 month' - '1 day'` |
| PostGIS | `min(view_date)`, `max(view_date)` | `(date_trunc('month', d) + interval '1 month - 1 day')::date` |
| Python | `deter["view_date"].min()` | `date + pd.offsets.MonthEnd(0)` |
| Power BI (DAX) | `MIN()`, `MAX()` | `EOMONTH ( date, 0 )` |
